title: Captain Pearl's Ship Log
text:
Monday. My name is Captain Pearl, and today my crew and I set sail on the good ship Sneezy Pickle. The sky was blue and the wind smelled like {food}. My first mate, a parrot named Gus, sat on my {body part} and sang songs about {plural noun} all morning.

Tuesday. We found a treasure map inside an old {noun}. The map says to sail past the {adjective} rock and then hop {number} times. Gus got so excited that he {past tense verb} around the deck until lunch.

Wednesday. We dug a big hole on Banana Beach. At the bottom was a wooden chest full of shiny gold coins and two {adjective} {plural noun}. We will share them with everyone in town. Tonight the whole crew is {verb ending in ing} under the stars. Being a pirate is very {adjective}.

title: Rules for the Good Ship Barnacle
text:
Welcome aboard the Barnacle! Captain Rosa is happy to have you on her crew. Please read these rules before we sail.

Rule one: Always wear your pirate hat, even at bedtime. If you lose your hat, you must wear a {noun} on your head until we find it.

Rule two: Never let the parrot eat {plural noun}. The last time that happened, he {past tense verb} on the mast for {number} days.

Rule three: Please do not {verb} near the treasure map. It is very old and very {adjective}.

Rule four: Every pirate must say "Ahoy, {plural noun}!" when they wake up in the morning.

Rule five: Dinner is at six o'clock. Cook Marco is making {adjective} soup with extra {food} again. Eat it {adverb} and say thank you.

If you follow every rule, you get to steer the ship and wear the captain's {adjective} coat.

title: Help Wanted: Parrot Sitter
text:
HELP WANTED! Captain Fizz is going on a treasure hunt and needs someone to take care of his parrot, Professor Feathers.

Professor Feathers is {number} years old and very {adjective}. He eats crackers and a small bowl of {plural noun} every morning. After breakfast, he likes to sit on a {noun} and sing sea songs {adverb}. He knows all the words except one, so he just yells "{silly word}!" instead.

The right person must be able to {verb} and whistle at the same time. You must also be good at {verb ending in ing}, because Professor Feathers gets bored very fast. Please do not let him near the captain's {plural noun}. He hides them in his nest.

Pay is one gold coin a day and all the {food} you can eat. If you want the job, please {verb} three times next to the ship and wave a {adjective} flag.

title: Letter Home from Pirate Camp
text:
Dear Mom and Dad,

Pirate Camp is going great! On the first day, Captain Jo gave everyone a striped shirt and a {adjective} eye patch. My bunk is right next to the camp parrot, who squawks like a {animal} all night.

Every morning we practice tying knots and looking through a telescope. Yesterday I saw a whole island made of {plural noun}! Then we learned how to {verb} like a real pirate. Captain Jo said I was very {adjective} at it.

Today we went on a treasure hunt. We followed the map {adverb} and dug under a palm tree. Inside the chest we found {number} {plural noun} and a note that said "Good job, mateys!"

Please send more socks and a jar of {food}. I miss you, and I miss {verb ending in ing} in my own bed.

Love,
Sam

title: How to Read a Treasure Map
text:
So you found a treasure map! Good job. Here is how to use it.

Step one: Unroll the map {adverb}. Old maps are very {adjective} and can rip if you pull too hard.

Step two: Find the big red X. That is where the treasure is. If the X is next to a drawing of a {noun}, you are going the right way.

Step three: Count your steps. Most maps say something like "Walk ten steps past the {adjective} tree, then hop like a {animal}." Always do what the map says, even the hopping part.

Step four: Start {verb ending in ing}. Real pirates dig with a shovel, but my uncle Pete uses a {noun}.

Step five: Open the chest. Inside you might find gold coins, shiny jewels, or {number} {plural noun}. Last summer my sister found a whole box of {plural noun}. She {past tense verb} all the way home.

title: Pirate News at Six
text:
Good evening, and welcome to Pirate News at Six. I'm Polly Anchor.

Our top story tonight: Captain Bea and her crew have found the lost treasure of Pickle Island! The treasure was buried under a giant {noun} for {number} years. When the crew opened the chest, they found gold coins, silver cups, and a pile of {adjective} {plural noun}. Captain Bea was so happy that she {past tense verb} right there on the sand.

In other news, the town parrot contest was held today. The winner was a parrot named Kiwi, who can say "{exclamation}" and {verb} at the same time. The judges said Kiwi was the most {adjective} bird they had ever seen.

Now for the weather. Tomorrow will be sunny with a chance of {plural noun} in the afternoon. Sailors should bring a {noun} and sail {adverb}. Good night, mateys!

title: Cook Marigold's Famous Ship Stew
text:
Every Friday on the good ship Snapdragon, Cook Marigold makes her famous ship stew. The whole crew lines up with their bowls. Here is her secret recipe.

You will need one big pot, three carrots, one {adjective} potato, and a cup of {food}.

First, fill the pot with water and stir it {adverb} with a wooden spoon. Next, add the carrots, the potato, and a spoonful of {plural noun}. Let it bubble for one hour. While you wait, you can {verb} around the kitchen.

When the stew turns {color}, it is ready. Cook Marigold always adds a tiny pinch of {plural noun} at the very end. She says that is the secret.

Serve it hot with a slice of bread. The crew says it tastes like a {adjective} {noun}. Last Friday, Captain Lou ate three bowls and then {past tense verb} until bedtime.

title: A Chat with Captain Crackers
text:
Today our class newspaper is talking to Captain Crackers, the oldest parrot on Coconut Bay.

Q: Hello, Captain Crackers! How old are you?
A: I am {number} years old. That is very old for a parrot.

Q: What is your favorite thing about being a pirate parrot?
A: I love sitting on the captain's {body part} and looking for treasure. Also, the snacks. Our cook makes {adjective} crackers with {plural noun} on top.

Q: Have you ever found real treasure?
A: Yes! Once I found a chest full of {plural noun} buried under a {noun}. The captain {past tense verb} with joy.

Q: Can you say any words?
A: I can say "Hello," "Ahoy," and "{silly word}." I am learning to {verb}, too, but it is hard with wings.

Q: Any advice for young pirates?
A: Always be {adjective}, brush your feathers {adverb}, and never forget your {noun}.

title: Postcard from Treasure Island
text:
Dear Grandpa,

Greetings from Treasure Island! Our pirate ship got here on Tuesday after sailing for {number} whole days. The water here is {color} and the sand feels like {plural noun} between my toes.

This morning Captain Nell let me hold the treasure map. We walked past a waterfall and a very {adjective} cave until we found the big X. I dug {adverb} for an hour. Inside the chest were old coins, a golden spoon, and a {adjective} {noun}. The captain was so happy that she {past tense verb} all the way back to the ship.

Tonight we are having a beach party. Everyone is {verb ending in ing} around the campfire, and the ship's parrot is wearing a tiny {noun} on his head. I wish you could {verb} with us.

Love,
Maya

title: Lost and Found on the Jolly Muffin
text:
Attention, crew of the Jolly Muffin! This is your captain speaking. Our Lost and Found box is full again, so please listen carefully.

We found one striped sock, two eye patches, and a {adjective} {noun} under the map table. If they belong to you, please come and get them.

Someone left {number} {plural noun} in the captain's hammock. That is not a good place for them. They made the hammock very {adjective}.

Also, our parrot, Sunny, has been {verb ending in ing} on the mast since breakfast. We think he wants his {noun} back. If you borrowed it, please return it {adverb}.

Last of all, whoever used the cooking pot to bury treasure, please {verb} to the deck right away. Cook Ada needs it to make {food} for dinner.

Thank you, crew. Now let's all shout "{exclamation}!" and get back to work.
